market_commentary:
Canadian and global equity benchmarks advanced in the week ending April 9 — the S&P/TSX Composite closed at 33,478 (+1.12% W/W, +41.10% Y/Y)11, while the S&P 500 added +3.68% to 6,82512 and the Nikkei 225 gained +4.78% to 56,30830. The Canadian dollar firmed +0.70% to 0.7235 CAD/USD13, and the Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% for a seventh meeting1. The database tracks 5,644 active and proposed projects valued at $864.6 billion5.

Commodity moves split the pipeline along energy and metals lines — Brent crude fell -11.47% on the week to US$96.52/bbl, still +47.40% Y/Y10, against 28 oil and gas projects ($50.6B) and 207 power and energy projects ($328.1B)5. Gold settled at US$4,783/oz (+2.82%)15, copper at US$5.75/lb (+3.32%)16, and the Sprott uranium proxy at US$50.93 (+4.15%)17, referenced by 265 mining projects totalling $117.8B5. The 2s10s Government of Canada spread held at +63 bp with the 10-year at 3.58%2, against 657 rate-sensitive residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects ($76.4B)5.
